analysis.title: Nasdaq Longs Haven't Capitulated Despite The AI Meltdown
key_insights: Nasdaq is within its broader trading range but has already broken below its 100-day moving average. The 200-day and the longer-term rising trendline are the next technical references.
Futures level 29k is flagged as the make-or-break level for Nasdaq.
NDX has sharply underperformed the Russell 2000 over the past 7-8 sessions, one of the sharpest stretches of tech underperformance versus small caps in a long time.
Goldman data shows non-dealers bought $3.3bn of Nasdaq futures between October 6 and 13 while the index fell 2.1%. Short covering of $7.3bn more than offset $4bn of long liquidation.

Non-dealer Nasdaq futures positioning entered the latest selloff at the 94th percentile of its two-year range, so no comparable washout has occurred despite the AI selloff in memory, neoclouds and hyperscalers.

Nasdaq futures open interest rose a net $1.4bn as hyperscalers joined the AI selloff, mostly around the October 16 decline. The funding premium versus the S&P 500 disappeared and implied volatility and put skew jumped.
On October 19 Nasdaq stabilized, relative funding recovered, and both volatility and skew retreated. Bearish hedges were abandoned quickly once prices steadied.
Three-month implied volatility and 25-delta put skew rose together in the selloff and then reversed with the bounce.
VXN spiked in the selloff and is now neither cheap enough to make downside protection attractive nor expensive enough to make volatility selling compelling, unless the NDX range is expected to hold.
NDX had been ignoring widening CDS spreads but is now responding to credit stress, which remains active. AI-related credit concerns continue to linger.
Heading into earnings, AI leadership is damaged, futures positioning is elevated and downside hedges have started to unwind. The setup is described as binary.
earnings_insights: Nasdaq enters earnings with damage across AI leadership, elevated futures positioning and unwinding hedges. If earnings fail to stabilize the index, crowded positioning could add selling pressure. A recovery through key technical levels could force another round of short covering.
risk_factors: Crowded Nasdaq futures positioning could add selling pressure if earnings fail to stabilize the index.
Equities are now responding to widening CDS spreads and AI-related credit stress.
A break below the 29k futures level, and then the 200-day moving average and rising trendline, would extend the decline.
